slides.headline: LINKEDIN PULLED ITS AI WRITER
slides.body: The platform removed its "enhance your post" feature, which let AI write entire posts for you. It's being replaced by a basic proofreading tool that only checks your grammar. Even LinkedIn admitted their own tool helped create the slop problem

slides.headline: YOU CAN NOW REPORT AI POSTS
slides.body: LinkedIn is rolling out a "seems like AI slop" button on every post so anyone can flag AI-written content. The company says fighting slop is "a top priority." They block hundreds of thousands of automated comments every single day

slides.headline: YOUR ACCOUNT GETS SECRETLY FLAGGED
slides.body: If your content looks fake, LinkedIn will quietly put a warning on your account without telling you why. New AI tools will scan posts before they reach your feed. Substack added its own AI detection tool last week through a deal with Pangram

slides.headline: HALF THE INTERNET ISN'T EVEN HUMAN
slides.body: Cloudflare says bot traffic now exceeds real human traffic across the entire web, and Digg shut down its Reddit competitor in March because bots took over. If your business pastes AI writing into every post, you're next. The companies winning use AI to run their operations behind the scenes, not to fake their voice

slides.headline: LINKEDIN WON'T BE THE LAST
slides.body: Every major platform is watching what happens here. Follow so you see who cracks down on AI content next. Send this to the person who pastes ChatGPT into every LinkedIn post
